device.manufacturer: NIIMBOT (Wuhan Jingchen Intelligent Identification Technology Co., Ltd., FCC ID 2ARXB)
device.name: NIIMBOT D110 / B21 Thermal Label Printer
device.notes:
Popular cheap thermal label printer with a closed ecosystem. $15-30. D110 is a compact single-label printer; B21 adds larger print width and more features. The community open-source client "NiimBlue" (Web Bluetooth) has reverse-engineered the full protocol through MultiMote/niimbluelib.
PROTOCOL: packet-based binary protocol over BLE GATT. Each packet uses 0x55 0x55 as header and 0xAA 0xAA as tail. Packet structure: [prefix(optional)] [0x55 0x55] [command] [data_length] [data...] [checksum] [0xAA 0xAA].
CHECKSUM: XOR of all bytes from command through the last data byte (inclusive). For simple request packets (data_length=1, data=1), checksum equals the command byte.
PACKET TYPES: - 0xC1 Connect / 0xC2 response (connection handshake, only packet
  with 0x03 prefix)
- 0x01 PrintStart (1-9 byte variants depending on model) - 0x13 SetPageSize (2-13 byte variants) - 0x03 PageStart / 0xE3 PageEnd - 0xF3 PrintEnd - 0x21 SetDensity / 0x31 response - 0x23 SetLabelType / 0x33 response - 0x84 PrintEmptyRow (fill row with white pixels) - 0x85 PrintBitmapRow (send row with black/white pixel data) - 0x83 PrintBitmapRowIndexed (row with < 7 black pixels, uses pixel
  indexes)
- 0xDC Heartbeat / 0xDD, 0xDE, 0xDF and 0xD9 responses (0xD9 =
  Advanced2, the normal response on protocol-v3+ printers)
- 0x40 GetDeviceInfo — multiple response IDs for different info
  (serial, hardware, firmware, etc.)
- 0x28 PrinterReset / 0x38 response - 0xF5 StartFirmwareUpgrade ([major, minor] version bytes in the
  ordinary XOR envelope; reply 0xF6). The image itself then travels in
  a CRC32-checked variant of the envelope (0x91 FirmwareCrc, 0x9B
  FirmwareChunk, 0x9C no more chunks, 0x92 FirmwareCommit).

D110 SPECIFIC: uses 1-byte PrintStart variant. SetPageSize uses the 4-byte [rows(u16), cols(u16)] BIG-endian variant (the 2-byte row-count-only variant is the old D11, not the D110). Printhead is 96px wide (12mm @203dpi, 12 bytes/row for 1-bit data) — NOT 384px; 384px/48mm is the B21 printhead.
BITMAP ROW ENCODING: PrintBitmapRow (0x85) sends row data with a black-pixel-count segment. For rows with fewer than 7 black pixels, PrintBitmapRowIndexed (0x83) sends pixel x-coordinates as uint16 BIG-endian values (Utils.u16ToBytes; wiki example x=320 = 01 40) instead of a full bitmap.
HEARTBEAT: send 0xDC with data [0x01] or [0x04] (protocol version dependent). Response includes lid closed status, charge level, paper inserted, RFID status, and (on newer models) ribbon state.
DISCOVERY: advertised names are model-prefixed ("D110-*", "B21-*", "D11-*"). niimbluelib filters a scan on the service UUID plus the first letter of each model name; other implementations match model-name prefixes; none matches a "NIIMBOT" prefix — do not scan for "NIIMBOT". Service UUID is manufacturer-specific; niimbluelib handles service/char discovery dynamically.
FIRMWARE / ECOSYSTEM (verified 2026-07-31): the community archive fw.niim.blue hosts original, unmodified official firmware (D110 up to v13.15, B21 up to v1.31); D110 images are raw (base 0x01010000) and newer files carry a 0x18-signature header with length + CRC32 fields. D110 MCU is a YiCHiP YC3121-d (D110_M: YC3122-L, refuses downgrades). The vendor cloud API is live without auth: POST print.niimbot.com/api/firmware/machineCascadeDetail returns per-model characteristics. Newer "v4" models (D110_M, B21_PRO, D11_H) use a different print task — 9-byte PrintStart, 13-byte SetPageSize, no PageStart — so the uniform-protocol assumption is aging. Consumable lock-in: paper/ribbon RFID tags (RfidInfo 0x1A/0x1C, WriteRFID 0x70, AntiFake 0x0B) plus a region lock are documented on the wiki.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for packet format, checksum algorithm, command IDs, PrintStart/SetPageSize variants, bitmap row encoding, and heartbeat format — sourced from MultiMote/niimbluelib, the production-quality TypeScript library behind niim.blue, tested against D110, B21, B1, D11, and other NIIMBOT models.

factory_reset.effect: Send PrinterReset packet (0x28); the printer answers 0x38. niimbluelib's comment on the packet calls it a reset of printer settings (sound, and possibly others); whether it clears anything more, or amounts to a factory reset, is not established.

procedures.basis: niimbluelib's packet generator names 0x28 PrinterReset with reply 0x38 and describes it as resetting settings such as sound; not run by this project.
procedures.name: Command reset

methods.description: Scan for model-prefixed advertisement, connect, send connect handshake, then start print sequence.

steps.action: Scan for a model-prefixed name ("D110-*", "B21-*") and connect.
Send Connect packet (0xC1) and receive response (0xC2).
Begin print sequence: SetDensity → SetLabelType → PrintStart → PrintClear → PageStart → SetPageSize → SetPrintQuantity → print rows → PageEnd → poll PrintStatus → PrintEnd.

setup.notes: Connect, send Connect packet (0xC1), then begin print sequence. No pairing or bonding required.

rejoin.notes: No bonding. Any central can connect.

variants.notes: 96px printhead (12mm @203dpi, 12 bytes/row). 1-byte PrintStart. 4-byte SetPageSize [rows(u16), cols(u16)] big-endian.

Larger print width (384px/48mm printhead). Same 1-byte PrintStart and 4-byte SetPageSize as the D110, but niimbluelib runs it as its own task: no PrintClear and no SetPrintQuantity (the page is sent once per copy), total-mode black-dot counts, check lines on, and the job ends by polling PrintEnd until its 0xF4 reply carries 1. (The 7-byte PrintStart / 6-byte SetPageSize belong to the B1-family task, not the B21.)
Similar to D110. 1-byte PrintStart; old D11 uses the 2-byte SetPageSize.

entities.name: Battery Level
entities.notes: 0-4 gauge step from the D110 heartbeat reply; a consumer must send the heartbeat request to get one, and must only decode replies whose response_id is 0xDD (see the characteristic notes). Scoped to the D110 because the B21's heartbeat is a different length with the byte elsewhere.

entities.name: Lid Closed
entities.notes: On = lid closed (the D110 reports 1 with the lid shut; see the lid_closed field for the inversion niimbluelib applies by model id). Same heartbeat-reply caveats as Battery Level.

entities.name: Paper
entities.notes: Unbound: the D110's 10-byte heartbeat reply has no paper byte (niimbluelib reports paper only for the 13-, 19- and 20-byte replies of other models), so on the namesake model this reading cannot be produced. Declared so the gap is visible; see remaining_unknowns.

enter.notes: niimbluelib names packet 0xF5 StartFirmwareUpgrade: an ordinary XOR-envelope packet whose two data bytes are the image's major and minor version, answered by 0xF6. The image then goes in a CRC32 variant of the envelope — 55 55 <cmd> <index u16 BE> <len> <data> <crc32 u32 BE> AA AA — for 0x91 FirmwareCrc, 0x9B FirmwareChunk, 0x9C no more chunks and 0x92 FirmwareCommit. None of it is declared as a command: the sequence has not been run here, and a client that builds it must treat it as advanced.

image.format: Raw application image (D110 base address 0x01010000); newer files carry the 0x18-signature header with length and CRC32 fields described in device.notes.
image.notes: The community archive https://fw.niim.blue hosts original, unmodified official images (D110 up to v13.15, B21 up to v1.31). Whether the bootloader checks anything beyond the CRC32 is not established. The D110_M (YC3122-L) refuses downgrades.

dfu.notes: From MultiMote/niimbluelib and the fw.niim.blue archive; not exercised by this project. The same packet protocol also runs over Bluetooth Classic serial (SPP) and USB serial, and whether the upgrade packet works on those transports is not established. The print service carries every ordinary command too, so it is not listed under `services`.

niimbot_print_task.black_dot_counts: The three count bytes before `repeat` count the row's black dots. When the row's bytes fit three chunks of floor(head_dots/8/3) bytes — always on the D110: 12 bytes, chunks of 4 — each count byte is the black dots in its chunk, in order ("split" mode). A row too wide for that sends the total instead: niimbluelib emits [0x00][total low byte][total high byte] — see remaining_unknowns. niimbluelib also falls back to the total form when it does not know the head width; a client of this spec knows it from print_geometry.
niimbot_print_task.check_line: 0x86 PrinterCheckLine ([row u16][0x01]) at rows 199, 399, … (every 200th row; the printer answers 0xD3) is optional in niimbluelib and off by default; not part of this task.
niimbot_print_task.example: An indexed row as niimbluelib documents it: 55 55 83 0E 00 7E 00 04 00 01 00 27 00 28 00 29 00 2A FA AA AA — row 126, split counts 0/4/0 (four black dots, all in bytes 4-7), repeat 1, black dots 39-42, checksum 0xFA.
niimbot_print_task.print_direction: niimbluelib's D110 model prints "left": a label designed landscape (long side along the feed) is sent with canvas column x as wire row x and the canvas's bottom edge at head dot 0. That is a rotation the client chooses; the wire only sees rows across the 96-dot head.
niimbot_print_task.replies: Every control packet is answered on the Print Data characteristic by a fixed reply id: connect 0xC1→0xC2, set_density 0x21→0x31, set_label_type 0x23→0x33, print_start 0x01→0x02, print_clear 0x20→0x30, page_start 0x03→0x04, set_page_size 0x13→0x14, set_print_quantity 0x15→0x16, page_end 0xE3→0xE4, print_status 0xA3→0xB3, print_end 0xF3→0xF4. A client waits for each reply before sending the next packet. 0xDB is a print error and 0x00 means the printer does not support the command it was sent. Row packets (0x83, 0x84, 0x85) get no reply; niimbluelib still leaves 10 ms between consecutive BLE writes (its issue 5), rows included.
niimbot_print_task.rows:
A page is sent as rows across the head, top of the feed first, row index from 0. A wire row is head_dots/8 = 12 bytes on the D110, MSB of byte 0 = head dot 0, 1 = black. Consecutive identical rows are sent once with a repeat count. Repeat is one byte, so a client splits a run longer than 255 rows into packets of at most 255 (that rule is this spec's: niimbluelib does not cap the count, and a 256-row run would wrap to 0). Three packet shapes, row and index fields u16 big-endian:
  0x84 PrintEmptyRow: data = [row u16][repeat u8] — len 3; the rows are
    all white.
  0x85 PrintBitmapRow: data = [row u16][count0][count1][count2]
    [repeat u8][12 row bytes] — len 18 on the D110.
  0x83 PrintBitmapRowIndexed: data = [row u16][count0][count1][count2]
    [repeat u8][index u16 ...] — one big-endian dot index per black
    dot. Only for rows with at most 6 black dots; niimbluelib records
    that a printer powers off when sent more.
niimbot_print_task.source: MultiMote/niimbluelib (MIT) — its D110 print task, packet generator, command map, image encoder and packet parser. Reported, not run by this project: testing.status stays untested until a D110 prints from it.
niimbot_print_task.status_reply: 0xB3 data: [page u16 BE][print_progress u8][feed_progress u8], at least 4 bytes (8 or 10 on some firmware). The counter is the number of COPIES finished in the job so far — cumulative across pages, not a page index. After each page's page_end a client polls print_status about every 300 ms until the counter equals the running total of the set_print_quantity values it has sent, before the next print_clear or the final print_end (niimbluelib compares for equality, so a counter that overshot would make it time out rather than finish). Each poll waits up to 5 s for its reply and is retried once, so about 10 s of silence ends the job. (One page at quantity 3 is done at 3, not 1.)

remaining_unknowns:
niimbluelib also runs this D110 task for D11 units on protocol v1 (96-dot head; its table lists v2 too, but its own negotiation never assigns that version) and for the 384-dot B21S, but whether a given D11 is one of those is only known from its firmware reply; the print surface is scoped to the D110 until a D11 has been identified that way.
The whole print task is reported from niimbluelib, not run here: reply timing, whether rows need more pacing over BLE than niimbluelib's 10 ms between writes, and what the printer does if print_end arrives before print_status reports the page.
The 0xB3 print-status reply carries an error byte only in its 10-byte form, at data offset 6 per niimbluelib's parser; its codes are not recorded here.
The black-dot "total" count form is emitted by niimbluelib low byte first ([0x00][lo][hi]) although every other u16 in the protocol is big-endian; whether that is what the printer reads or a quirk nothing exercises is not established. The D110 never uses it (its 12-byte rows always fit split mode).
The Print Data characteristic multiplexes every reply, and the schema has no frame selector: the format block is written for the D110's 17-byte heartbeat reply (0xDD, 10 data bytes) and a consumer has to check response_id and data_length itself before using the lid and charge offsets.
Other models' heartbeat replies put the same facts elsewhere — per niimbluelib, a 13-byte data field (B1) carries lid at data byte 9, charge at 10, paper-inserted at 11 and RFID-read at 12; a 19-byte field has them at 15-18; a 20-byte field carries only paper at 18 and RFID at 19 — and one offset table cannot hold all four, so the Battery Level and Lid entities are scoped to the D110 and the B21 has no bound readings.
Paper presence is not in the D110 heartbeat reply at all, so the Paper entity has nothing to bind on the namesake model; whether the D110 reports it through another query is not established.

connect.description: 0xC1 handshake, the one packet sent with a leading 0x03. Replies 0xC2.

heartbeat.description: 0xDC Heartbeat. Type 1 (advanced 1), or 4 (advanced 2) on protocol v3 and later; the D110's 0xDD reply is decoded by this characteristic's format block. Type 3 asks for printer info (head width, versions); a D110 answers it with 0x00, not supported.

checksum.description: XOR of cmd, len and data; encoder-filled.

print_clear.description: 0x20 PrintClear — clears the page buffer before each page. Replies 0x30.

print_end.description: 0xF3 PrintEnd — finishes the job, sent once the PrintStatus poll completes; niimbluelib also sends it after an error or timeout, so the job ends either way. Replies 0xF4.

print_status.description: 0xA3 PrintStatus — polled after PageEnd until the page is done. Replies 0xB3; layout in protocol_details.niimbot_print_task.

set_density.description: 0x21 SetDensity — print darkness, first step of a job. Replies 0x31.

checksum.description: XOR of cmd, len and data; encoder-filled.

density.description: Darkness level; the codes are declared on the image_upload feature's print_density.

set_label_type.description: 0x23 SetLabelType — the loaded stock, second step of a job. Replies 0x33.

checksum.description: XOR of cmd, len and data; encoder-filled.

label_type.description: Stock code; declared on the image_upload feature's paper_type.

set_page_size.description: 0x13 SetPageSize, the D110's 4-byte variant: rows then columns, each u16 big-endian. Replies 0x14.

checksum.description: XOR of cmd, len and data; encoder-filled.

cols.description: Dots across the head, a multiple of 8.

rows.description: Rows in the page — the label's length along the feed, in dots.

set_print_quantity.description: 0x15 SetPrintQuantity — copies of the page about to be sent, u16 big-endian. Replies 0x16.

checksum.description: XOR of cmd, len and data; encoder-filled.

format.name: response_id
format.notes: The layout below only holds for 0xDD.

format.name: data_length
format.notes: 10 on the D110; other values mean another model's heartbeat layout.

format.name: lid_closed
format.notes: Data byte 8 of the D110 heartbeat: 1 = lid closed, 0 = open. The raw byte's sense is inverted on the D110 relative to most models: niimbluelib reads 0 as closed and then flips it for a list of model ids that includes the D110's primary id 2304 (but not its second id 2305), and its capture of a real D110 on firmware 13.14 reads 1 here with the lid shut. A consumer that cannot read the model id should trust the D110 reading as written here.

format.name: charge_level
format.notes: A five-step gauge (data byte 9), not a percent; the labels are the steps' nominal fill. The same 0-4 code comes back from the battery-level printer-info query. niimbluelib's heartbeat parser labels this byte a percentage; the 0-4 scale the printer-info query returns is the reading adopted here, so treat a value above 4 as a percent from a newer firmware.

characteristics.name: Print Data
characteristics.notes: Single characteristic for command writes AND responses/heartbeat notifications on most models (niimbluelib selects the char requiring NOTIFY + WRITE_NO_RESPONSE). FRAME SELECTION: every reply the printer sends arrives here in the `55 55 <cmd> <len> <data...> <xor> AA AA` envelope, and the format block below describes exactly one of them — the reply to the 0xDC heartbeat request as a D110 sends it: cmd 0xDD with a 10-byte data field, 17 bytes in all. Check bytes 2-3 read 0xDD 0x0A before trusting the offsets; a print acknowledgement or an info reply on the same characteristic puts other bytes there. Offsets are from niimbluelib's heartbeat parser (the 10-byte case: lid at data byte 8, charge level at data byte 9, no paper field) — reported, not read back by this project. Other models answer with 13-, 19- or 20-byte data fields whose lid/charge/paper bytes sit elsewhere; see remaining_unknowns.

services.name: NIIMBOT Print Service
services.notes:
Most models expose service e7810a71-73ae-499d-8c15-faa9aef0c3f2 with a single characteristic carrying both directions (niimbluelib still discovers service/char dynamically). The packet-based binary protocol is consistent across all pre-v4 NIIMBOT models, and the same protocol also runs over Bluetooth Classic serial (SPP) and USB serial (115200 baud); the printer exposes two BT addresses (BLE + classic).
PACKET FORMAT: `[0x03?] 0x55 0x55 <cmd> <len> <data...> <xor_checksum> 0xAA 0xAA` The 0x03 prefix is used only on the Connect packet (0xC1). Checksum = XOR of cmd through last data byte.
PRINT SEQUENCE (D110 task, per niimbluelib's D110 print task): 1. Connect (0xC1) — handshake 2. SetDensity (0x21) — print density level 3. SetLabelType (0x23) — label/gap/continuous 4. PrintStart (0x01) — 1-byte variant 5. PrintClear (0x20) — clear the page buffer 6. PageStart (0x03) — begin page 7. SetPageSize (0x13) — [rows(u16), cols(u16)] big-endian 8. SetPrintQuantity (0x15) — copies of this page, u16 big-endian 9. PrintBitmapRow (0x85) / PrintBitmapRowIndexed (0x83) / PrintEmptyRow (0x84) 10. PageEnd (0xE3) — end page 11. Poll PrintStatus (0xA3) until its counter reaches the copies sent
    so far in the job (the running total of SetPrintQuantity values)
12. PrintEnd (0xF3) — finish job Every control packet is acknowledged; rows are not. See protocol_details.niimbot_print_task.
D110 MODEL: PrintStart uses 1-byte variant `55 55 01 01 01 <cs> aa aa`. SetPageSize uses the 4-byte big-endian variant `55 55 13 04 <row_hi> <row_lo> <col_hi> <col_lo> <cs> aa aa` (the 2-byte row-count-only variant is the old D11). D110 printhead is 96px (12mm @203dpi) — 384px is the B21.
